pr_title: fix(junit reporter): Properly report actual errors in the junit failure message property
pr_body:
Currently junit test failure are reported with the failing test file's name, failure location, and test name in the message property, while the actual failure information is stored in the CDATA text. This can break tools that look at the error message to do failure analysis and deduplication as they will not have the actual failure cause.

This change makes it so we report all unique errors hit by the tests in the xml failure entry's message property.

Fixes: #12944

issue_context.title: [BUG] Incorrect serialization failure message in Junit reporter
comments:
@Gornostalev The actual failure should be a text node child of the `<failure>` tag:
```xml
<failure message="example.spec.ts:5:3 Check equal" type="FAILURE">
  example.test.js:5:3 › Check equal =====================================================

    Error: Error message
    ......
</failure>
```
Is that text missing for you?
@dgozman, i know about this, but attribute message parsed for results in pipeline azure devops, and on screenshot field "Error message" not contain error message, it just a test title: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30836610/159529311-fcf370b9-a43f-4305-9a13-a596f551a8bd.png)
Thank you for the screenshot, this makes sense.

Ideally, we would make the following improvements:
- Use `<error>` element for thrown errors, and `<failure>` element for `expect` failures.
- For errors:
  * Put `error.name` in `type=""` attribute for errors.
  * Put error message in `message=""` attribute.
- For failures (expects):
  * Put `expect.toBe` in `type=""` attribute.
  * Put (possibly custom) expect message in `message=""` attribute.

review_comments: This way the message does not contain `file:line` information anymore which will likely break more tools than it will fix?

I don't really see what value of including the file given that you already know what test file and the test name are in the `testcase` parent node of the result entry. I would even argue that tools should be using that instead of relying on the file to be in the error message (not a direct relation)

For the line and column though, I would agree it's still useful to have in the error message and can add that back. Maybe enhance it with the actual function that threw?

Re: test name, if we remove the test location from the error, I believe it would make sense to add it to the `classname` in `<testcase classname="a.test.js:10:13">` instead. This will aid tools in navigating to the source, particularly when the test name is templated, such as "test(`test ${i}`...". In cases like these, a specific substring like 'test 5' may not exist in the file. What do you think?

> For the line and column though, I would agree it's still useful to have in the error message and can add that back. Maybe enhance it with the actual function that threw?

Yes, I think having text of the line that threw along with its location would be ideal, i.e. instead of the test location it would be actual error location. How about for the error that is currently formatted like:

```xml
<testcase name="one" classname="a.test.js" time="0.133">
<failure message="expect(received).toBe(expected) // Object.is equality  Expected: 0 Received: 1
New failure on retry 2" type="FAILURE">
<![CDATA[  a.test.js:3:15 › one ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    Error: expect(received).toBe(expected) // Object.is equality

    Expected: 0
    Received: 1

      5 |               throw new Error('New failure on retry 2');
      6 |             }
    > 7 |             expect(1).toBe(0);
        |                       ^
      8 |           });
      9 |         

        at fn (/Users/yurys/playwright/test-results/reporter-junit-created-should-render-all-unique-errors-after-retry-playwright-test/a.test.js:7:23)
...
```

We change it to the following?

```xml
<testcase name="one" classname="a.test.js:3:15" time="0.133">
<failure message="a.test.js:7:23 expect(received).toBe(expected) // Object.is equality  Expected: 0 Received: 1
New failure on retry 2" type="FAILURE">
<![CDATA[  a.test.js:3:15 › one ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    Error: expect(received).toBe(expected) // Object.is equality

    Expected: 0
    Received: 1

      5 |               throw new Error('New failure on retry 2');
      6 |             }
    > 7 |             expect(1).toBe(0);
        |                       ^
      8 |           });
      9 |         

        at fn (/Users/yurys/playwright/test-results/reporter-junit-created-should-render-all-unique-errors-after-retry-playwright-test/a.test.js:7:23)

```

Or alternatively add the location to the end of the message, e.g. `message="a.test.js:7:23 expect(received).toBe(expected) // Object.is equality  Expected: 0 Received: 1
New failure on retry 2 at a.test.js:7:23"`
